- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 73+ → 75+) are common, followed by exaggerated downward corrections.
- Model underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 60–65 range) and overestimates mid-range (65–75) — exhibits bias toward higher values.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often dips below forecast by day 10–15, then slowly catches up.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in price drops — often forecasts a rebound when true price continues falling.
- In cases of strong downward trends, model overcorrects upward, creating false “recovery” signals.
- Model exhibits poor sensitivity to recent low-price data — ignores recent 5–7 day downtrends in favor of longer-term averages.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to reflect volatility spikes or sudden policy-driven price shifts.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, leading to “false momentum” in forecasts when actual price corrects downward.
